sources.title: Did They Tweet That? repository README

users.description: The group member who launches the app and gets a one-phone party session to its first valid answer.
The player holding the phone outward who cannot perceive the active card, makes the single physical tilt-or-tap commit, and contributes to the group result without individual score ownership.
The friends who see and read the active statement, discuss and relay the collective judgment, and share the forehead-mode group result.
The current local player or team member who privately sees and commits an answer, owns the player or team score, and hands off without exposing prior content or outcome.
A participant who requires tap-only, no-motion, screen-reader, reduced-motion, color-independent, no-audio, or no-haptic play while retaining role, privacy, score, answer, and truth-review semantics.
The operator who sources, previews, verifies, approves, publishes, reviews reports about, and removes cards.

tasks.description: Reach a valid first answer with one phone, minimal setup, and no facilitator explanation.
Know who can perceive the content, who may commit an answer, whose score changes, which control is active, what remains private, and what happens next.

Perceive or receive an attributed statement according to the active role, discuss when social play applies, and register exactly one intended authentic-or-fabricated guess without leaking protected card information.
Continue the same round after sensor, motion, orientation, interruption, or connectivity failure without losing state or duplicating an answer.
After guessing, identify whether the statement is authentic, fabricated, disputed, removed, or unavailable and understand the product's truth posture.
Rematch or hand the phone to the correct next player without losing pace, score, or turn ownership.
Report an incorrect, harmful, offensive, or rights-sensitive card and return to the same review context, including while offline.
Preview realistic cards, record evidence, apply safety rules, publish a version, triage reports, and remove content within policy targets.

claims.text: The repository contains planning documents and an early Expo/React Native scaffold under apps/mobile; its expansion remains blocked until the signed implementation gate permits it.
The intended MVP is a local one-phone party game rather than a news product, public UGC platform, or realtime multiplayer product.
Phase 0 is intended to test forehead and tap play with one bundled editorial deck, no accounts, and no backend dependency.
Every played card requires an explicit post-answer authenticity state, and fabricated content must be identified as made for the game.
Bundled or cached party play must remain available without network access.
Tap-only, no-motion, and screen-reader players must be able to complete the same core round and truth-review tasks.
Stakeholders propose at least 70 percent of Phase 0 groups completing two or more rounds unaided, at least 80 percent control usability, and at least 40 percent Phase 1 rematch rate.
The mobile scaffold uses Expo and React Native with TypeScript, but no qualified LaunchPad browser lane or approved styling system exists yet.

assumptions.description: Forehead play creates enough additional social energy and memorability to justify motion complexity and role asymmetry.

validation.hypothesis: At least four of six representative group sessions will identify compensating social value in forehead play over the equivalent tap countermodel without a material increase in unrecovered task failure.
killCriteria: More than one of six moderated group sessions has an unrecovered forehead-path failure that does not occur in the tap countermodel.
A majority of moderated group sessions prefer the tap countermodel and cannot identify compensating social value in forehead play.

assumptions.description: A new group can understand roles and controls and reach a valid first answer with little or no facilitation.

validation.hypothesis: At least five of six moderated group sessions will reach a valid first answer without moderator instruction beyond the prepared study prompt.
killCriteria: Two or more of six group sessions require moderator explanation to identify who sees the card, who may answer, or how the active player commits.
Any repeated setup step causes two or more group sessions to abandon or restart before the first valid answer.

assumptions.description: Explicit reveal language can restore trust after the game intentionally withholds authenticity during the guess.

validation.hypothesis: After review, at least 80 percent of participating individuals will correctly explain each tested authentic, fabricated-for-game, disputed, source-unavailable, and removed state without relying on color alone.
killCriteria: More than 20 percent of participating individuals describe a tested fabricated card as verified or real after its completed reveal state.
Any active pre-reveal, review, or share capture permits a fabricated attribution to appear without its game-round context or its completed fabrication meaning, as applicable.

assumptions.description: Representative statement lengths and attributions can be understood quickly from the viewing distances, angles, and lighting of group play.

validation.hypothesis: At least five of six moderated group sessions will correctly read representative short, median, and maximum-length cards at the predeclared test distance and lighting before the selected decision window expires.
killCriteria: Two or more of six group sessions cannot correctly read a median-length card at the predeclared distance and lighting.
Any territory requires hiding attribution, truth status, or a critical control to fit representative maximum-length content.

assumptions.description: Tap-only and screen-reader paths can preserve task completion, truth understanding, scoring, and the social rhythm of the core game.

validation.hypothesis: Participants who regularly use screen readers or non-motion controls will complete their role-appropriate setup, full round, results, and review without leaked forehead-card information, missing truth information, or different scoring semantics.
killCriteria: Any required non-motion or screen-reader path cannot complete the same role-appropriate round, result, and truth-review sequence as the default path.
Any forehead-holder screen-reader path exposes the active statement before review, or any accessible participant requires sighted or motion-capable assistance for a designated primary task.

assumptions.description: The team can supply enough safe, funny, sourceable, representative content to validate the interaction and later sustain multiple decks.

validation.hypothesis: Before direction testing, an accountable editorial owner will approve a representative set covering length, difficulty, authenticity, fabrication, sensitivity, source, disputed, removed, and offline conditions.
killCriteria: No accountable editorial owner or two-person review path exists before participant direction sessions begin.
The study cannot use representative approved content without relying on unreviewed harmful fabrication or an unresolved source-rights pattern.

assumptions.description: The proposed 18 to 28 friend-group audience is the most promising launch segment for the one-phone authenticity party ritual.

validation.hypothesis: Observed Phase 0 groups in the proposed launch segment will complete and rematch at the stakeholder-defined thresholds, yielding a recorded product-owner go/no-go decision before direction approval.
killCriteria: Observed Phase 0 behavior does not meet the stakeholder-defined completion and rematch thresholds for the proposed segment.
No product-owner go/no-go decision is recorded against the predeclared Phase 0 protocol and segment.

assumptions.description: A persistent, content-neutral game-round marker can keep every pre-reveal state recognizable as play when captured without revealing authenticity.

validation.hypothesis: All ordinary screenshots, recordings, and photographs of tested active pre-reveal states will retain the game-round context marker while revealing no authenticity outcome or source-authority cue.
killCriteria: Any tested active pre-reveal capture can be reasonably read as an authentic public statement because it lacks a game-round context marker.
Any proposed context marker discloses authenticity, source status, or editorial confidence before the answer.

unknowns.description: No interviews, group observations, usability sessions, or accessibility participant evidence exists for this product.
unknowns.rationale: Strategy may proceed with bounded hypotheses, but direction approval requires the registered validation evidence.

unknowns.description: Trademark, publicity, defamation, copyright, store-policy, and fabrication patterns have not received counsel approval.
unknowns.rationale: Problem framing and reversible exploration may proceed, but implementation claims and store release remain blocked pending counsel decisions.

unknowns.description: The allowed source, storage, display, and deletion pattern for authentic statements is unresolved.
unknowns.rationale: Strategy can define trust states without asserting a legal solution, but representative content and implementation need an approved rights pattern.

unknowns.description: No accountable editorial owner, monthly capacity, or participant-study content approver is identified.
unknowns.rationale: Strategy can proceed, but direction validation cannot begin until the editorial-readiness kill criteria are cleared.

unknowns.description: Launch markets, languages, age rating, content filters, and analytics-consent rules are undecided.
unknowns.rationale: Initial strategy is locale-agnostic, while handoff and release must resolve the applicable content and consent requirements.

unknowns.description: The LaunchPad lane matrix does not qualify Expo React Native, and no project-owned native verification configuration exists.
unknowns.rationale: The current artifact-only proposal can proceed, but implementation and release need iOS and Android task, sensor, accessibility, offline, lifecycle, and performance evidence.

unknowns.description: The representative viewing distance, lighting, angle, device-size matrix, capture conditions, and content/state fixture have not been frozen for comparison.
unknowns.rationale: Territory generation may wait for strategy review, and the independent direction-validation plan must freeze these conditions before sessions so territories are compared on the same task and state pressure.

unknowns.description: No participant recruitment plan commits to people who regularly use screen readers or non-motion controls.
unknowns.rationale: Direction approval requires participant evidence for the role-specific screen-reader and non-motion paths; an evaluator-only script cannot clear the accessibility-equivalence assumption.

unknowns.description: The named product, research, accessibility, and editorial decision owners have not yet accepted their study responsibilities.
unknowns.rationale: Direction validation cannot begin until the product owner, research lead, accessibility lead, and editorial owner are recorded against the predeclared protocol and fixture.

directionCriteria.description: The direction must enable a new group to reach a valid first answer without hidden product knowledge or moderator instruction.
directionCriteria.measurement: Use the same prepared prompt and representative setup in every territory; record assistance, restarts, abandonment, and time to first valid answer.

directionCriteria.description: The direction must preserve statement, attribution, time status, and required control meaning across representative content and group viewing conditions.
directionCriteria.measurement: Test short, median, and maximum-length content at predeclared phone sizes, distances, angles, and lighting; record correct first-read completion.

directionCriteria.description: The direction must register one intended answer, make control readiness understandable, and provide a recoverable non-motion path.
directionCriteria.measurement: Compare accidental answers, duplicate commits, control misunderstandings, fallback use, and unrecovered failures across the candidate and countermodel.

directionCriteria.description: The direction must make authentic, fabricated, disputed, removed, and source-unavailable meanings explicit after the guess without relying on color or platform imitation, and must retain content-neutral game context before the guess.
directionCriteria.measurement: Ask individual participants to explain each completed truth state in their own words and inspect ordinary pre-reveal, review, and share captures for detached false-attribution risk.

directionCriteria.description: The direction must support role-appropriate primary-round, result, review, and report outcomes through tap-only and screen-reader-compatible paths without breaking forehead-card privacy.
directionCriteria.measurement: Run role-specific critical-task scripts with participants who regularly use screen readers or non-motion controls through motion, tap-only, VoiceOver, and TalkBack paths; compare completion, privacy, information, scoring, timing choice, and recovery semantics.

directionCriteria.description: The direction should minimize setup and transition friction while keeping current actor, turn ownership, and next action clear.
directionCriteria.measurement: Compare setup time, transition hesitation, assistance, handoff errors, rematch choice, and participant comments using the same content and session structure.

directionCriteria.description: The direction should feel specific to a social authenticity-guessing ritual without reproducing social-feed chrome, news authority cues, or generic trivia conventions.
directionCriteria.measurement: Ask evaluators what the experience is specifically about, what evidence supports that interpretation, and whether any authority cue could misrepresent fabricated content.

directionCriteria.description: The direction must explain playable, offline, loading, corrupt, interrupted, sensor-failed, disputed, removed, queued-report, and recovery conditions without dead ends.
directionCriteria.measurement: Walk the frozen fixture's non-normal states through an executable recovery path and fail any territory that loses round context, blocks available offline play, leaks a protected handoff, or lets disputed, source-unavailable, or removed content remain a binary playable claim.

directionCriteria.description: The direction must be feasible within planned Expo React Native performance, offline, sensor, content-size, and native accessibility constraints.
directionCriteria.measurement: Require engineering review against startup, frame-rate, sensor, offline, package-size, memory, lifecycle, and native accessibility constraints before handoff approval.

directionCriteria.description: The direction must allow realistic cards and all trust states to be previewed, reviewed, reported, and removed without one-off design exceptions.
directionCriteria.measurement: Pressure-test the same representative content set and operational states, then require editorial review of preview accuracy, source meaning, and removal behavior.

directionCriteria.description: The direction must make local debug logging, future analytics, and queued reporting compatible with the documented data-minimization and privacy contract.
directionCriteria.measurement: Inspect the fixture's report, offline, error, and settings paths to confirm raw motion, statement content, identities, source URLs, transcripts, and free text are absent by default, while a queued report retains only the documented operational fields.
